input: Register for a half marathon in the spring

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The user's location determines which races are geographically accessible or preferred, completely changing which events are relevant.
Spring spans March through May; the specific month or date range narrows which races are still open for registration and fit the user's schedule.
Registration fees vary widely ($50–$200+); knowing the budget rules out certain premium or charity races.
Whether the user wants a local, destination, or a specific well-known race (e.g., a major city race) changes the search entirely.
If the user is registering with friends or a running group, logistics like wave starts, group registration, or matching pace groups become relevant.
Knowing whether the goal is to finish, hit a time target, or qualify for a longer race (e.g., a full marathon) affects which race format and course profile to prioritise.
Whether the user needs help finding races, or already has one in mind and just needs to complete the registration process, determines the very first action to take.

gold.taskTitle: Register for a spring half marathon race
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to find and register for a half marathon race taking place in spring.

questions.title: What city or region do you want to race in?
questions.description: Identifies the geographic area to focus the race search on.

questions.title: Which part of spring works best for you?
questions.description: Narrows the target date range within spring (March, April, or May) to match availability and training readiness.

questions.title: What is your maximum budget for the entry fee?
questions.description: Sets a price ceiling to filter out races that are too costly.

questions.title: Do you have a specific race already in mind?
questions.description: Determines whether the task starts with finding a race or jumping straight to registration.

questions.title: Are you registering solo or with other people?
questions.description: Affects whether group registration, matching corrals, or coordinating schedules needs to be part of the plan.

questions.title: Do you prefer a local community race or a large city event?
questions.description: Shapes the type and scale of race to search for — intimate local runs vs. major organised events with crowds and expo.

questions.title: What does a successful race look like for you?
questions.description: Clarifies whether the priority is finishing, achieving a time goal, or using this as a stepping stone to a longer race — which influences course and race selection.
